articles.title: Parts of Delhi under IMD red alert for rain, cloudy skies may delay moon sighting on Karwa Chauth | India News - Hindustan Times

articles.full_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Thursday issued red and orange alert over possible moderate to heavy rainfall for parts of Delhi-NCR on Thursday. It has also forecast cloudy skies on Karwa Chauth, raising concerns over the visibility of the moon in the evening.
According to the IMD’s nowcast, as of around 5:45 pm, a red alert is in place for North Delhi, North West Delhi, West Delhi and South West Delhi, while an orange alert has been issued for Central Delhi, North East Delhi and South East Delhi. Meanwhile, Gurugram is under a yellow alert until 6 pm.
The minimum temperature in the national capital is expected to settle at around 19 degrees Celsius, while the maximum is likely to reach 26 degrees Celsius on October 29.
Karwa Chauth rituals likely to be impacted
The unsettled weather could affect Karwa Chauth rituals, as women observing the fast traditionally wait for the moon to appear before breaking their fast.
Amateur weatherman Navdeep Dhaiya also warned that persistent showers and cloud cover could make the evening moon sighting difficult. Highlighting the likely impact across Delhi-NCR and neighbouring regions, he said, “Karwa Chauth fasting to be impacted by weather! Frequent spells of varied-intensity showers will continue throughout the day along with cloudy conditions in Delhi NCR, Haryana, West UP and Chandigarh. Moon sighting is not expected at night due to overcast conditions; plan accordingly.”
Moonrise time in Delhi
The moonrise time in Delhi today, October 29, is expected to be around 8:11 PM to 8:17 PM.
Delhi weather: 7-day forecast
Delhi is likely to witness moderate rain under generally cloudy skies on October 29, with the minimum temperature at 19 degrees Celsius and the maximum at 26 degrees Celsius, as per IMD's weekly forecast.
Thunderstorms accompanied by rain are forecast for October 30, when the minimum temperature is expected to be 17 degrees Celsius and the maximum to reach 27 degrees Celsius.
On October 31, partly cloudy conditions are likely to prevail, with the minimum temperature settling at 18 degrees Celsius and the maximum rising to 29 degrees Celsius.
The weather is expected to turn clear on November 1, with temperatures ranging from a minimum of 17 degrees Celsius to a maximum of 30 degrees Celsius.
Clear skies are likely to continue on November 2, as the minimum temperature dips to 16 degrees Celsius while the maximum remains at 30 degrees Celsius.
Delhi is forecast to experience clear weather on November 3, with the minimum temperature at 16 degrees Celsius and the maximum at 30 degrees Celsius.
The mainly clear conditions are expected to persist on November 4, with the minimum temperature remaining at 16 degrees Celsius and the maximum reaching 30 degrees Celsius.

articles.full_text:
Delhi red alert: Heavy rain to lash Delhi-NCR as IMD issues red and orange alerts with thunderstorms warning
Delhi red alert: Heavy rain to lash Delhi-NCR as IMD issues red and orange alerts with thunderstorms warning
The IMD has issued a weather warning valid on October 29, alerting Delhi residents to moderate thunderstorms, lightning, hail and gusty winds across multiple districts.
Delhi red alert: In a matter of alert for the residents, the national capital is bracing for another spell of unsettled weather on Thursday, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a district-level nowcast warning of moderate thunderstorms, lightning, rainfall and possible hailstorms across several parts of Delhi. According to the official IMD bulletin issued on Thursday, the nowcast is valid for three hours until 6:08 pm on October 29. The weather system is being driven by a combination of western disturbances and cyclonic circulations that continue to influence weather patterns across North India. Here are all the details you need to know about the red alert issued by the IMD for Delhi.
Delhi red alert: Area-wise weather impact
Hailstorm & Moderate Thunderstorm Alert: Moderate thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and hail are very likely over parts of Central Delhi, New Delhi, South West Delhi, West Delhi and North Delhi.
Moderate Rain & Lightning: Thunderstorms with lightning and moderate rainfall are expected in parts of South East Delhi, East Delhi, Shahdara, Central Delhi, North East Delhi, South Delhi, North West Delhi and West Delhi.
Light Rain & Gusty Winds: Areas in South East Delhi, East Delhi and South Delhi may experience light rain or light thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds reaching speeds of 30 to 40 kmph.
Karwa Chauth fasting to be impacted by weather!
Frequent spells of varied intensity showers will continue throughout the day along with cloudy conditions in Delhi NCR, Haryana, West UP and Chandigarh.
Moon sighting is not expected in night due to overcast conditions, plan accordingly.
#DelhiRains
Disaster management officials and meteorological authorities have advised residents to take precautions during lightning and hail activity and to stay updated via local weather bulletins.
Delhi’s air quality continued to remain in the ‘poor’ category
Delhi’s air quality continued to remain in the ‘poor’ category on Thursday morning, with the city-level Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 229, slightly above Wednesday’s reading of 228, according to the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) All India AQI portal.
Uttam Nagar reported the highest AQI at 339, followed by Mundka at 336 and Dwarka Sector 8 at 307. CRRI Mathura Road recorded an AQI of 297, while Jahangirpuri registered 294. Punjabi Bagh and Vivek Vihar reported readings of 286 and 277, respectively, a report by ANI said.
Lodhi Road recorded the lowest AQI among Delhi’s reporting stations at 129. Ghoga followed with a reading of 132, while IMD Lodhi Road registered 148. All three stations fell within the ‘moderate’ category.
